hypotheses.justification: The retained hqn implies n ≠ 0, since every natural number divides 0. Thus recover 0 < n and use the original proof; the zero case is impossible.

Take a finite Galois intermediate field K containing F₀, ζ and α, using adjoining and normal closure. Let σ be the restriction of primeLocalToGlobal q φ to K and r = orderOf σ. Finite.algHom and Finite.algEquiv give finiteness, so orderOf_pos and pow_orderOf_eq_one give r > 0 and σ^r = 1. Apply exists_level_dvd_of_frobenius_pow_mem_inertia_sup with base K and positive level r * (n * d), then take normal closure F. By H_anti, membership in H q F forces this level to divide m. Hence n*d divides m and σ^m = 1, which fixes α by AlgEquiv.restrictNormalHom_apply. This works even when q divides n.

The finite-order construction described for hqn works for arbitrary ζ: adjoin ζ and α to F₀, take finite normal closure K, and let r > 0 be the order of the restricted automorphism. Force r*(n*d) to divide the relevant exponents using exists_level_dvd_of_frobenius_pow_mem_inertia_sup, then take normal closure. These exponents fix α and are divisible by n*d. No root-of-unity property is needed; ζ = 0 also causes no problem.

Every α in AlgebraicClosure ℚ belongs to a finite Galois intermediate field K containing F₀ and ζ. The restriction of primeLocalToGlobal q φ to K has positive finite order r. Apply exists_level_dvd_of_frobenius_pow_mem_inertia_sup at level r*(n*d), and take normal closure. H_anti gives r*(n*d) ∣ m, so the restricted m-th power is the identity and fixes α. Thus the power equation is unnecessary, including when α = 0.
